thread:
sasha: quick update from the regional slicebench I ran yesterday — A100 vs H100 across 7B and 13B models (prefill+decode combined). summary first, details below.

derek: nice, hit me with the headline numbers.

sasha: 7B (fp16 -> bf16 pipeline): A100 ~900 tok/s, H100 ~1150 tok/s. 13B: A100 ~430 tok/s, H100 ~670 tok/s. numbers are steady-state decode (long-running, batching tuned). prefill costs add ~10-15% latency for typical prompts.

maria: those deltas look solid. what were the batch sizes and seq lengths?

sasha: batch=8, decode seq=128, prefill seq avg=512 (mix of short & long prompts). used continuous batching with max latency SLO=150ms for tail config.

kevin: how about $/1M tokens? that's what infra cares about.

sasha: rough econ using current spot SKU rates: 7B -> A100: $0.88 / 1M tokens, H100: $0.63 / 1M tokens. 13B -> A100: $1.95 / 1M, H100: $1.12 / 1M. includes GPU amortized cost + small infra overhead. H100 wins on cost for both sizes due to better throughput at similar core utilization.

derek: kernel stack used? quant? bnb?

sasha: tested three stacks: 1) native float16 with CUTLASS kernels (default), 2) TensorRT int8 (where available), 3) bitsandbytes 8-bit (bnb) for the 13B. For 7B, bnb + CUTLASS on H100 gave ~20% speedup over fp16 CUTLASS. For 13B, TensorRT int8 on H100 required extra tuning but gave ~40% throughput improvement vs A100 fp16.

maria: any quality regressions observed from int8/bnb?

sasha: ran 500 eval prompts (generation & next-token logprob checks). bnb-int8 on 7B: negligible quality diff on top-k accuracy and logprob delta <0.03 avg. TensorRT int8 on 13B: small cold-case hallucination uptick in ~4% of prompts (mostly longer-context arithmetic), flagged for further eval.

perf-bot: summary commit created: perf/bench/1943214000-slicebench (link) :slightly_smiling_face:

kevin: regional differences? europe vs us?

sasha: yes — eu-west1 H100 nodes were ~6-8% slower than us-west1 H100 for decode (likely network/firmware diff or power profile). cost in eu adds ~12% on $/1M due to higher instance price. still H100 in eu was cheaper than A100 in eu for 7B, margin smaller for 13B.

derek: tail latency numbers? 95/99?

sasha: 95p decode latency: 7B H100 ~28ms/token, A100 ~36ms/token. 99p: H100 ~48ms, A100 ~72ms. Prefill tail is bigger: 99p prefill ~1.2s on average (large prompts), so full request 99p can hit ~1.3-1.4s for worst mixes.

maria: any ops constraints? memory pressure on 13B with quantized kernels?

sasha: 13B TensorRT int8 needed slightly more host-side pinned memory during prefills (KV allocation pattern), so we bumped swap thresholds on a subset of nodes. Also saw occasional OOM on A100 when running aggressive batch=16 for 13B, so we pinned max batch to 12 for A100 and 16 for H100 in the recommendations.

kevin: suggested routing policy then?

sasha: propose default: prefer H100 for heavy decode workloads (>=7B) in us regions; fall back to A100 for bursty low-latency small prompt workloads where cost sensitivity higher. add region multiplier in cost estimator to show eu-us difference.

derek: can you paste the command snippet you used so eng-runtime can reproduce?

sasha: sure — here's the benchmark driver:

```
# run slicebench: parallel worker config, continuous batching, record prefill+decode latency
./bench_driver --model gpt-open-7b --batch 8 --prefill-seq 512 --decode-seq 128 \
  --kernel CUTLASS --quant fp16 --region us-west1 --workers 12 --duration 20m

# tensorRT run (13B)
./bench_driver --model gpt-open-13b --batch 12 --prefill-seq 512 --decode-seq 128 \
  --kernel TRT --quant int8 --tune --region us-west1 --duration 30m
```

maria: thanks — i'll queue the reproducer on our infra lab. any follow-ups we should track?

sasha: action items: 1) perf: run extended TRT int8 quality eval on 13B (maria) 2) infra: investigate eu H100 6-8% delta (kevin) 3) runtime: add region multiplier to cost estimator + default routing change (derek). I'll open PRs for numbers/bench results and upload logs.

kevin: noted. can you also add per-token cost calc snippet so pricing team can sanity-check?

sasha: will do — I'll attach the calc & raw CSV in the PR. quick calc used: effective_gpu_hours = runtime_seconds / 3600 * nodes; cost = effective_gpu_hours * sku_rate; tokens_per_run * runs -> 1M token extrapolation.

derek: awesome, clean and actionable. thanks Sasha. :thumbsup:

sasha: np, will ping when PR is up.
